fieldMarks: White-phase foxes are entirely white in winter and brown-gray above, paler below, in summer.
Blue-phase foxes stay dark or charcoal year-round with little seasonal change.
Paws are sheathed in dense fur in winter.
behavior: Does not hibernate; nomadic and can travel several hundred kilometres.
Summer diet centres on lemmings and voles; also takes seabirds, eggs, berries and scavenges seal remains from polar bear kills.
Caches surplus food in summer; dens have 4–8 entrances and are dug in sandy banks, hillocks and talus.
Monogamous pairs raise pups together; families break up in September–October.
habitat: Treeless Arctic and alpine tundra, usually coastal, often near rocky shores.
range: Arctic tundra of Canada, Alaska (Aleutians north to Point Barrow) and Greenland, and across Eurasian Arctic regions.

lookalikes.name: Red fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Red foxes have a white tail tip, black legs and reddish coats, and dominate arctic foxes where their ranges overlap.
